title: Health Signal Weighting Cheatsheet
content:
Health Signal Weighting Cheatsheet — v0.9 (working)

Purpose
- One-page working reference for the CS team to compute a consistent customer health index used in QBRs, renewal risk triage, and playbook routing.
- Focus: lightweight signals that are available weekly via analytics pipeline (no expensive manual inputs).
- This is intentionally opinionated: fewer signals, clear weights, explicit risk-flag rules.

Design principles - Parsimony: limit to ~10 signals so score is interpretable.
- Mix leading (engagement) and lagging (billing) indicators.
- Prefer continuous metrics with normalized bins, rather than many binary flags.
- Provide explicit overrides: technical blocker = immediate high-risk.

Signal categories and canonical metrics 1) Product usage (35 points total)
- Active seats (10): week-over-week % change in distinct users that sent >=1 API call in the last 7 days.
- Token throughput (10): 7-day rolling avg tokens/day normalized by customer contract baseline.
- Feature depth (15): % of endpoints used (generation, embeddings, reranking, streaming) weighted by product priority (e.g., production-gen=6, eval=2).

2) Platform health / reliability (20 points total)
- Error rate (10): percentage of requests returning 5xx or model-incompatible errors last 7d.
- Latency SLO breaches (5): count of SLO breach incidents last 30d normalized to 0-5 scale.
- Retry ratio (5): ratio of retried requests to total requests (indicator of transient failures).

3) Adoption & engagement (20 points total)
- Docs/events engagement (5): visits to docs + attendance at product webinars / workshops last 30d normalized.
- Support touch frequency (5): number of distinct support threads opened by customer in last 30d (too low can be silent churn, too high implies friction).
- Feature requests vs PRs (10): ratio of product-accepted suggestions or beta enrollments to requests opened (measures constructive collaboration).

4) Commercial signals (15 points total)
- Billing trend (10): 30d $ usage vs contract baseline (negative trend reduces score).
- Contract stage (5): near renewal (<=90d) get small positive boost if other signals healthy; overdue/in arrears set hard high-risk.

5) Security & compliance (10 points total)
- Alerts / audit log anomalies (5): any new compliance escalations in last 90d.
- Private deployment issues (5): open infra tickets for VPC/on-prem that block production.

Normalization & scoring rules - Each signal is normalized to 0-100 then multiplied by its point budget, summed to a 0-100 health index.
- Example bins (apply to token throughput):
  - >=110% of baseline -> 100; 90-110% -> 80; 50-90% -> 50; 10-50% -> 20; <10% -> 0.
- Error rate: 0-0.5% -> 100; 0.5-2% -> 60; 2-5% -> 20; >5% -> 0.
- Make all normalization functions configurable in the analytics layer; defaults are conservative (favor flagging risk).

Hard risk flags (immediate override to score <=20)
- Any P1 outage in last 7 days impacting prod inference.
- Customer account in billing collection or legal review.
- Data loss or confirmed security incident.

Soft risk flags (subtract 10 points each)
- Sustained week-over-week decline in active seats >10% for 4 consecutive weeks.
- No API calls for 14+ days for customers previously active.
- Major regression detected in observed output quality (model-eval alerts).

Tier cutoffs & suggested actions
- Healthy (>=70): prep QBR, upsell motion where usage growth observed, push advanced features.
- Watch (50-69): schedule AM touchpoint, share adoption recipes, run health checklist.
- Risk (21-49): CS owner to open Renewal Playbook, coordinate with solutions engineering for adoption workshop, check billing & security.
- Critical (<=20): immediate escalation — SRE, sales, legal as appropriate. Freeze self-serve trials if fraud detected.

Quick scoring example (simplified)
- Customer A (mid-market)
  - Active seats: 95% of baseline -> normalized 80 -> points 8 (of 10)
  - Token throughput: 120% baseline -> 100 -> points 10 (of 10)
  - Feature depth: using 2/4 core endpoints weighted -> normalized 50 -> points 7.5 (of 15)
  - Error rate: 0.8% -> normalized 60 -> points 6 (of 10)
  - Latency SLO breaches: 0 -> normalized 100 -> points 5
  - Support touches: 1 thread (healthy) -> normalized 80 -> points 4
  - Billing trend: flat -> normalized 80 -> points 8
  - No hard flags -> total = 48.5/100 -> Watch.

Implementation checklist (analytics + CS ops)
- Analytics: implement weekly ETL that produces signal table with columns: customer_id, week_start, active_seats_pct_of_baseline, tokens_pct_of_baseline, endpoints_used_count, error_rate_pct, slo_breaches_count, support_threads_30d, billing_pct_of_baseline, security_alert_flag, p1_last_7d_flag.
- CS ops: map scores to dashboards and automate Slack alerts for <=50 and for any hard flags.
- QBR template: include the top 3 negative signals and the playbook steps taken.

Column spec for tracking sheet (simple to copy to Sheets)
- customer_id
- customer_name
- week_start
- health_index (0-100)
- top_3_negative_signals (comma separated)
- hard_flag (yes/no)
- CS_owner
- next_action_due
- renewal_date
- notes

Operational notes / open questions
- Should we weight private deployments higher in feature depth? (PRO: deeper integration; CON: skews large on small non-prod customers).
- How to incorporate qualitative signals from CSM notes? (short-term: store binary 'recent-proactive-touch' but exclude text parsing until we have NLP pipeline).
- Frequency: compute weekly; surface daily only for P1 or billing-critical incidents.

Change log
- 2025-11-10 created by Avery (baseline signals list).
- 2026-01-22 added Feature depth metric and feature-weighting idea (Maya).
- 2026-03-12 moved error-rate bins to more conservative thresholds after pilot (Liam).

TODOs (short term)
- [ ] Analytics: materialize endpoints_used_count in events pipeline (ticket JIRA-CS-4890).
- [ ] CS: run backfill for last 90 days and validate risk buckets for 50 largest accounts.
- [ ] Product: finalize weights for feature depth and share final CSV mapping.

Notes to self
- This sheet should be the single source of truth when prepping playbooks; avoid adding too many ad-hoc signals per customer — prefer cataloging as \"custom flags\" outside of default health index.

End of doc — comments welcome.
